title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the first draft of Grothendieck's combinatorial 'Analysis situs' (1986). He sets up an axiomatic theory of 'figures': a set of figures F ordered by inclusion '<=' and satisfying axioms C1-C3 (defined on earlier pages). The irreducible figures M (the 'strata' or cells) generate everything else.

The page first states a representation theorem, completing p.60. Restrict to systems (F,<=) satisfying C1-C3 in which every figure is 'finite', meaning it has finitely many subfigures, or equivalently finitely many strata. These systems correspond exactly to triples (M, <=, R), where:
- <= is a partial order on M;
- R is a reflexive, symmetric 'compatibility' relation;
- (a) every principal down-set M_{<=x} is finite;
- (b) R is downward closed: if (x,y) in R and x'<=x, y'<=y, then (x',y') in R.
Under this correspondence the figures are the finite down-closed subsets A of M whose elements are pairwise R-compatible. Going back, M is the set of irreducible figures. Page 60 shows each figure is a union of principal ones M_{<=x_i} over finitely many mutually compatible x_i.

The page then treats connected components:
- A figure F is connected if, whenever F = F' u F'' with F' n F'' empty, one of F', F'' equals F.
- F is 0-connected if it is connected and nonempty. The empty figure is connected under this definition, hence the separate notion, in line with Grothendieck's usual care about the empty object.
- A subfigure F_0 is a connected component of F if F_0 is 0-connected and F = F_0 ⊔ G for some G disjoint from F_0.
- Lemma: if F = F' ⊔ F'' and G is a connected subfigure of F, then G lies in F' or in F''. The proof, continued on p.62, decomposes G as G' ⊔ G'' with G' in F' and G'' in F''.

Page 62 derives that two components are equal or disjoint. It also identifies the components of F with the connected components of its set of strata in the order (Alexandrov) topology.

Purpose: this builds the combinatorial skeleton of a 'tame topology' in which stratified spaces are described by finite posets of strata with a compatibility relation.
errors: In the lemma, 'soit G une sous-figure connexe de G' is a slip for 'de F'.

The connectedness definition is stated loosely, with the disjointness hypothesis added as an insertion. As written it makes the empty figure connected, which Grothendieck handles by introducing '0-connexe'. This is consistent, not an error.
The component definition is unfinished: clause (b) is crossed out, and the requirement that G be disjoint from F_0 is only implicit in the ⊔ notation.

The representation theorem is asserted, not proved, on this page. Its proof relies on pp.57-60 (each figure is a finite union of principal figures of pairwise compatible elements) and looks correct under the stated finiteness hypotheses.

ideas.what: Systems of finite figures satisfying C1-C3 are equivalent to triples (M,<=,R): a poset with finite principal down-sets and a reflexive, symmetric, downward-closed compatibility relation. Figures are the finite down-closed, pairwise-compatible subsets.
ideas.modern_name: Prime event structure with binary conflict (conflict = complement of R) and its finite configurations; equivalently, the poset of compact elements of a prime-algebraic, finitary, coherent domain. When <= is trivial it reduces to the clique complex of a graph, or the finite cliques of a coherence space.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen-Plotkin-Winskel (1981) for event structures and their domain representation; Winskel (1980s); Girard (1986-87) for coherence spaces.
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this poset/compatibility formalism does not appear there.

ideas.what: Connected and 0-connected figures (the empty figure is connected but not 0-connected), connected components as 0-connected direct summands, and the lemma that a connected subfigure lies in one summand of a disjoint decomposition.
ideas.modern_name: Connected components in an extensive / coproduct-decomposition setting; connected components of a down-set in the Alexandrov topology.
ideas.where_published: The connected vs. nonempty-connected distinction appears in SGA1/SGA4 style (connected objects of a Galois category or topos), but not in this form.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's characterization of finite 'figure systems' is, after replacing R by its complement, exactly Winskel's prime event structures with binary conflict. The axioms match one for one: finite causes = 'M_{<=x} finis'; conflict inherited upward = condition (b); configurations = finite down-closed conflict-free sets = his figures. His identification of (F,<=) with (M,<=,R) is the finitary half of the Nielsen-Plotkin-Winskel representation theorem, found independently in 1986 for tame-topology purposes. The concurrency literature and the Grothendieck literature appear never to have linked the two.
missed.quote: (M, ≤, R) où ≤ relation d'ordre, R relation réfl. et symm., satisfaisant à a) les M_{≤x} finis b) si (x,y)∈R et x'≤x, y'≤y, alors (x',y')∈R, où les figures sont les parties ... finies de M telles que ... (x,y)∈R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a geometric (stratified-space) reading of event structures and of the directed-topology / higher-dimensional-automata approach to concurrency. Conversely, it offers Grothendieck's analysis-situs program a ready-made, well-developed domain theory (stable functions, rigid maps) as its morphism theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically the page is elementary: a representation theorem plus routine connectedness lemmas. But the exact coincidence with prime event structures, discovered independently in a tame-topology context around the time Girard introduced coherence spaces, is a genuine and apparently unrecorded cross-field connection.
transcription_corrections: Figure clause should read roughly: 'où les figures sont les parties A de M, [les parties fermées finies de M], telles que pour tous x, y ∈ A on ait (x,y) ∈ R.'
Lemma: 'soit G une sous-figure connexe de G' should read 'de F'.
Component definition: 'F = F_0 ⊔ G', with a crossed-out 'G connexe' replaced by 'F_1 disjoint de F_0'.

Left margin begins 'Ou F = F' ⊔ F''', introducing the ⊔ notation for disjoint unions of figures; the rest of the margin note on components ('Chaque composante ... disjointe ...') is largely illegible.
Long diagonal crossed-out passage in the middle of the page, about the compatibility relation and strata x, y ∈ A; it is cancelled and largely illegible.
